nodes.name: Lehmer's conjecture
nodes.statement: Lehmer's conjecture~\cite{Leh} asserts that there is an absolute constant $C>0$ such that if~$f(X)\in\ZZ[X]$ is a monic polynomial of degree~$D\ge1$ whose roots are not roots of unity, then \begin{equation} \sum_{f(\a)=0} h(\a) \ge C. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: There is an absolute $C>0$ with $\sum_{f(\a)=0}h(\a)\ge C$ for every monic $f\in\ZZ[X]$ of degree $\ge1$ whose roots are not roots of unity.
nodes.section: Introduction
assumptions: if~$f(X)\in\ZZ[X]$ is a monic polynomial of degree~$D\ge1$ whose roots are not roots of unity,
conclusions: \sum_{f(\a)=0} h(\a) \ge C.

nodes.name: Theorem of Borwein, Dobrowolski and Mossinghoff on polynomials congruent to $1$ modulo $m$
nodes.statement: \textup{(Borwein, Dobrowolski, Mossinghoff \cite{BoDoMo})} Let $m\ge2$, and let $f(X)\in\ZZ[X]$ be a monic polynomial of degree~$D$ that satisfies \begin{equation} f(X) \equiv X^D+X^{D-1}+\cdots+X^2+X+1 \pmod{m}. \end{equation} Then \[ \sum_{f(\a)=0} h(\a) \ge \frac{D}{D+1}C_m, \] where we may take \[ C_2 = \frac{1}{4}\log5 \quad\text{and}\quad C_m = \log\frac{\sqrt{m^2+1}}{2}\quad\text{for $m\ge3$.} \]
nodes.statement_short: If every coefficient of a monic degree-$D$ $f$ is $\equiv1\pmod m$, then $\sum h(\a)\ge\frac{D}{D+1}C_m$ with an explicit $C_m$.
nodes.section: Introduction
assumptions: Let $m\ge2$
let $f(X)\in\ZZ[X]$ be a monic polynomial of degree~$D$ that satisfies \begin{equation} f(X) \equiv X^D+X^{D-1}+\cdots+X^2+X+1 \pmod{m}. \end{equation}
conclusions: \sum_{f(\a)=0} h(\a) \ge \frac{D}{D+1}C_m,
where we may take \[ C_2 = \frac{1}{4}\log5 \quad\text{and}\quad C_m = \log\frac{\sqrt{m^2+1}}{2}\quad\text{for $m\ge3$.} \]

nodes.name: Lehmer's conjecture for polynomials divisible modulo $m$ by $X^{n-1}+\cdots+X+1$
nodes.statement: For all $\e>0$ there is a constant $C_\e>0$ with the following property\textup: Let $f(X)\in\ZZ[X]$ be a monic polynomial of degree~$D$ such that \begin{equation} \text{$f(X)$ is divisible by $X^{n-1}+X^{n-2}+\cdots+X+1$ in $(\ZZ/m\ZZ)[X]$} \end{equation} for some integers \[ m\ge2\qquad\text{and}\qquad n\ge\max\{\e D,2\}. \] Suppose further that no root of~$f(X)$ is a root of unity. Then \[ \sum_{f(\a)=0} h(\a) \ge C_\e\log m. \] In particular, Lehmer's conjecture~\eqref{eqn:lehmerconj} is true for this class of polynomials.
nodes.statement_short: For each $\e>0$, monic $f$ divisible mod $m$ by $\F_{n-1}$ with $n\ge\max\{\e D,2\}$ and no root of unity satisfy $\sum h(\a)\ge C_\e\log m$.
nodes.section: Introduction
assumptions: Let $f(X)\in\ZZ[X]$ be a monic polynomial of degree~$D$ such that \begin{equation} \text{$f(X)$ is divisible by $X^{n-1}+X^{n-2}+\cdots+X+1$ in $(\ZZ/m\ZZ)[X]$} \end{equation}
for some integers \[ m\ge2\qquad\text{and}\qquad n\ge\max\{\e D,2\}. \]
Suppose further that no root of~$f(X)$ is a root of unity.
conclusions: \sum_{f(\a)=0} h(\a) \ge C_\e\log m.
In particular, Lehmer's conjecture~\eqref{eqn:lehmerconj} is true for this class of polynomials.

nodes.name: Elliptic Lehmer conjecture
nodes.statement: The elliptic analogue of Lehmer's conjecture says that if~$E/K$ is an elliptic curve defined over a number field, then there is a constant $C_{E/K}>0$ such that for all nontorsion points $Q\in E(\Kbar)$ of degree $D_Q=[K(Q):K]$ we have \begin{equation} D_Q \hhat_E(Q) \ge C_{E/K}. \end{equation} Here~$\hhat_E$ is the logarithmic canonical height on~$E$.
nodes.statement_short: For $E/K$ there is $C_{E/K}>0$ with $D_Q\hhat_E(Q)\ge C_{E/K}$ for every nontorsion $Q\in E(\Kbar)$.
nodes.section: Introduction
nodes.origin_citation: elliptic analogue of Lehmer; cf. Hindry & Silverman, Laurent, Masser
assumptions: if~$E/K$ is an elliptic curve defined over a number field, then there is a constant $C_{E/K}>0$ such that for all nontorsion points $Q\in E(\Kbar)$ of degree $D_Q=[K(Q):K]$
conclusions: D_Q \hhat_E(Q) \ge C_{E/K}.

nodes.name: Elliptic Lehmer conjecture under an elliptic mod $\gm$ condition
nodes.statement: Let $K/\QQ$ be a number field and let~$E/K$ be an elliptic curve. Fix some $\e>0$. Then the elliptic Lehmer conjecture~\eqref{eqn:ellipticlehmer} is true for all points~$Q\in E(\Kbar)$ satisfying an elliptic mod~$\gm$ condition analogous to~\eqref{eqn:fXdivXn1X1ZmZ} for some ideal~$\gm$ such that $\Norm_{K/\QQ}\gm\ge2$ and such that~$E$ has good reduction at all primes dividing~$\gm$ and for some $n\ge\max\{\e{D_Q},2\}$. The lower bound in~\eqref{eqn:ellipticlehmer} will have the form $C_{E/K,\e}\log m$.
nodes.statement_short: The elliptic Lehmer conjecture holds for points satisfying an elliptic analogue of the mod-$\gm$ divisibility condition, with bound of size $C_{E/K,\e}\log m$.
nodes.section: Introduction
assumptions: Let $K/\QQ$ be a number field and let~$E/K$ be an elliptic curve.

The lower bound in~\eqref{eqn:ellipticlehmer} will have the form $C_{E/K,\e}\log m$.

nodes.name: Comparison with Samuels' congruence-condition height bounds
nodes.statement: Our Theorem~\ref{thm:intromultgp} and some of Samuels' principal results~\cite{MR2313990} are height bounds for polynomials satisfying various sorts of congruence conditions, so we conclude this introduction by briefly describing how the results differ. Our polynomials satisfy a divisibility condition modulo~$m$, so multiplying by~$X-1$, our theorem applies to polynomials~$F(X)$ of the form \[ F(X) = (X^n-1)A(X) + mB(X)\qquad\text{for some $A,B\in\ZZ[X]$.} \] In general, we obtain a bound for all~$n$ (see Lemma~\ref{lemma:htgeelogm}), and in particular we prove Lehmer's conjecture if~$n\ge\e\deg(F)$. The results in~\cite{MR2313990} apply to (factors of) polynomials that are congruent modulo~$m$ to a simpler polynomial of the same degree. For example, a typical result in~\cite{MR2313990} is a bound for (noncyclotomic factors of) polynomials~$F(X)$ of degree~$nr$ satisfying \[ F(X) = (X^n-1)^r + mB(X)\qquad\text{for some $B\in\ZZ[X]$.} \] Thus although there is some overlap, our result and the results in~\cite{MR2313990} apply to largely different classes of polynomials. It might be interesting to combine the methods of the two papers to prove a general result encompassing both.
nodes.statement_short: Our divisibility condition mod $m$ and Samuels' congruence conditions cover largely different classes of polynomials.

nodes.name: Normalized absolute values, normalized valuations and the absolute logarithmic height
nodes.statement: We let $M_\QQ$ be the usual collection of absolute values on~$\QQ$, and for any algebraic extension~$K/\QQ$, we write~$M_K$ for the set of all extensions of these absolute values to~$K$. For~$\a\in\Qbar$ and~$v\in M_\Qbar$, we define a normalized absolute value by choosing a finite extension~$K/\QQ$ with~$\a\in K$ and setting \[ \|\a\|_v = |\a|_v^{[K_v:\QQ_v]/[K:\QQ]}. \] We also define a normalized valuation by \[ v(\a) = -\log\|\a\|_v. \] Then the absolute logarithmic height of~$\a$ is defined by \[ h(\a) = \sum_{v\in M_K} \max\bigl\{\log\|\a\|_v,0\bigr\}. \] We write $M_K^0$, respectively~$M_K^\infty$, for the set of nonarchimedean, respectively archimedean, absolute values in~$M_K$.
nodes.statement_short: Normalizes $\|\a\|_v=|\a|_v^{[K_v:\QQ_v]/[K:\QQ]}$, sets $v(\a)=-\log\|\a\|_v$, and defines $h(\a)=\sum_v\max\{\log\|\a\|_v,0\}$.
nodes.section: 1 A Reformulation of Property
nodes.origin_citation: Hindry & Silverman, Diophantine Geometry; Lang, Fundamentals of Diophantine Geometry

nodes.name: Product formula and the height of an algebraic integer
nodes.statement: With the above normalization we have the product formula \[ \prod_{v\in M_K} \|\a\|_v = 1\qquad\text{for all $\a\in K^*$.} \] In particular, if~$\a\in K$ is a nonzero algebraic integer, then \[ h(\a) = \sum_{v\in M_K^\infty}\max\bigl\{\log\|\a\|_v,0\bigr\} = \sum_{v\in M_K^0} v(\a). \] We also remark that \[ \prod_{v\in M_K^\infty} \|\a\|_v = \prod_{v\in M_K^0} \|\a\|_v^{-1} = \Norm_{K/\QQ}(\a)^{1/[K:\QQ]}. \]
nodes.statement_short: With this normalization $\prod_v\|\a\|_v=1$, so for a nonzero algebraic integer $h(\a)$ equals both the archimedean and the nonarchimedean sum.
nodes.section: 1 A Reformulation of Property

nodes.name: Mahler measure as a sum of heights
nodes.statement: Let $f(X)\in\ZZ[X]$ be a monic polynomial. Then the classical Mahler measure~$M(f)$ of~$f$ is related to the heights of its roots via the formula \[ \log M(f) = \sum_{f(\a)=0} h(\a). \] In this paper we use the ``sum the heights'' notation because it has an obvious generalization to other algebraic groups such as elliptic curves. In such sums, we always include the roots of~$f$ with their multiplicities.
nodes.statement_short: $\log M(f)=\sum_{f(\a)=0}h(\a)$; the paper uses the sum-of-heights notation because it generalizes to other algebraic groups.
nodes.section: 1 A Reformulation of Property

nodes.name: The polynomial $\F_n(X)$
nodes.statement: For notational convenience, we let \[ \F_n(X) = X^n+X^{n-1}+\cdots+X+1. \] If~$n$ is prime, this is the usual cyclotomic polynomial; in general it is a product of classical cyclotomic polynomials.
nodes.section: 1 A Reformulation of Property

nodes.name: Weakenings of the mod $m$ divisibility property
nodes.statement: Let $m,n\ge2$, and let~$f(X)\in\ZZ[X]$ be a monic polynomial of degree~$D$. Consider the following three conditions\textup: \begin{parts} \Part{(i)} \text{$f(X)$ is divisible by $\F_{n-1}(X)$ in $(\ZZ/m\ZZ)[X]$.} \vspace{1\jot} \Part{(ii)} $m^{n-1} \mid \Resultant\bigl(f(X),\F_{n-1}(X)\bigr)$. \vspace{1\jot} \Part{(iii)} $\displaystyle \sum_{v\mid m} \sum_{f(\a)=0} v(\a^{n}-1) \ge (n-1)\log m$. \end{parts} Then \[ \textup{(i)} \Longrightarrow \textup{(ii)} \Longrightarrow \textup{(iii)}. \] \textup(In~\textup{(iii)}, we may work over any field in which~$f$ factors completely. The way that we have normalized our absolute values ensures that the choice of field does not matter.\textup)
nodes.statement_short: Divisibility of $f$ by $\F_{n-1}$ in $(\ZZ/m\ZZ)[X]$ implies $m^{n-1}\mid\Resultant(f,\F_{n-1})$, which implies $\sum_{v\mid m}\sum_{f(\a)=0}v(\a^n-1)\ge(n-1)\log m$.
nodes.section: 1 A Reformulation of Property
assumptions: Let $m,n\ge2$, and let~$f(X)\in\ZZ[X]$ be a monic polynomial of degree~$D$.
conclusions: Consider the following three conditions\textup: \begin{parts} \Part{(i)} \text{$f(X)$ is divisible by $\F_{n-1}(X)$ in $(\ZZ/m\ZZ)[X]$.} \vspace{1\jot} \Part{(ii)} $m^{n-1} \mid \Resultant\bigl(f(X),\F_{n-1}(X)\bigr)$. \vspace{1\jot} \Part{(iii)} $\displaystyle \sum_{v\mid m} \sum_{f(\a)=0} v(\a^{n}-1) \ge (n-1)\log m$. \end{parts} Then \[ \textup{(i)} \Longrightarrow \textup{(ii)} \Longrightarrow \textup{(iii)}. \]

nodes.name: Proof of the implications (i) $\Rightarrow$ (ii) $\Rightarrow$ (iii)
nodes.statement: Property~(i) says that \[ f(X) = \F_{n-1}(X)A(X) + mB(X) \quad\text{for some $A(X),B(X)\in\ZZ[X]$.} \] This implies that \begin{align*} \Resultant\bigl(f(X),\F_{n-1}(X)\bigr) &= \Resultant\bigl(\F_{n-1}(X)A(X) + mB(X),\F_{n-1}(X)\bigr)\\ &= \Resultant\bigl(mB(X),\F_{n-1}(X)\bigr)\\ &= m^{n-1} \Resultant\bigl(B(X),\F_{n-1}(X)\bigr). \end{align*} Thus~(ii) is true. \par We next prove that~(ii) implies~(iii). For any non-archimedean absolute value~$v$ we have \begin{align} \bigl\|\Resultant\bigl(f(X),x^{n}-1\bigr)\bigr\|_v &= \bigl\|\Resultant\bigl(f(X),\F_{n-1}(X)\bigr)\bigr\|_v \bigl\|f(1)\bigr\|_v \notag\\* &\le \|m\|_v^{n-1}. \end{align} \par A standard formula for the resultant~\cite[Section~V.10]{lang:algebra} is \begin{equation} \Resultant\bigl(f(X),X^{n}-1\bigr) = \prod_{f(\a)=0} (\a^{n}-1). \end{equation} We take the $v$-absolute value of~\eqref{eqn:resproddef}, use~\eqref{eqn:resgemD}, and multiply over all~$v\mid m$ to obtain the estimate \begin{equation} \prod_{v\mid m} \prod_{f(\a)=0} \|\a^{n}-1\|_v \le \prod_{v\mid m} \|m\|_v^{n-1} = m^{-(n-1)}. \end{equation} Taking~$-\log(\,\cdot\,)$ gives~(iii).
nodes.statement_short: Direct resultant computation for (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii), then $v$-adic estimates on the resultant product formula for (ii)$\Rightarrow$(iii).
nodes.section: 1 A Reformulation of Property

nodes.name: Product formula for the resultant
nodes.statement: \Resultant\bigl(f(X),X^{n}-1\bigr) = \prod_{f(\a)=0} (\a^{n}-1).
nodes.section: 1 A Reformulation of Property

nodes.name: The quantity $\D(\Acal,m,n)$
nodes.statement: Let~$\Acal\subset\Qbar^*$ be a finite set of algebraic integers and let~$m$ and~$n$ be positive integers. We define \[ \Delta(\Acal,m,n) = \sum_{\a\in\Acal} \frac{1}{\log m} \sum_{v\mid m} \frac{1}{n} v(\a^n-1). \] The inner sum is over all $v\in M_K^0$ with $v\mid m$, where~$K$ is any number field containing~$\Acal$. Our normalization of the valuations in~$M_\Qbar$ implies that the sum is independent of the choice of~$K$.
nodes.statement_short: $\D(\Acal,m,n)=\sum_{\a\in\Acal}\frac{1}{\log m}\sum_{v\mid m}\frac1n v(\a^n-1)$, a normalized measure of how $m$-divisible the values $\a^n-1$ are.
nodes.section: 1 A Reformulation of Property

nodes.name: Monotonicity of $\D$ under powering
nodes.statement: Let $\Acal$ be a finite set of algebraic integers, let $j,m,n\ge1$ be rational integers, and let $\Acal^j=\{\a^j:\a\in\Acal\}$. Then \[ \D(\Acal^j,m,n) \ge \D(\Acal,m,n). \]
nodes.statement_short: Powering the set of algebraic integers cannot decrease $\D$: $\D(\Acal^j,m,n)\ge\D(\Acal,m,n)$.
nodes.section: 1 A Reformulation of Property
assumptions: Let $\Acal$ be a finite set of algebraic integers,
let $j,m,n\ge1$ be rational integers,
let $\Acal^j=\{\a^j:\a\in\Acal\}$.
conclusions: \D(\Acal^j,m,n) \ge \D(\Acal,m,n).

nodes.name: Proof of monotonicity of $\D$ under powering
nodes.statement: From the factorization \[ X^{jn}-1 = (X^n-1)\F_{j-1}(X^n), \] we see that \[ v(\a^{jn}-1)=v(\a^{n}-1)+v(\F_{j-1}(\a^n))\ge v(\a^{n}-1) \] for any algebraic integer~$\a$ and any nonarchimedean absolute value~$v$. Summing over $\a\in\Acal$ and $v\mid m$, and then dividing by~$n\log m$, gives the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Factor $X^{jn}-1=(X^n-1)\F_{j-1}(X^n)$ to get $v(\a^{jn}-1)\ge v(\a^n-1)$, then sum and normalize.
nodes.section: 1 A Reformulation of Property

nodes.name: Property (iii) restated as $\D(\Acal_f,m,n)\ge (n-1)/n$
nodes.statement: We observe that if $f(X)\in\ZZ[X]$ is a monic polynomial of degree~$D$ and if we write~$\Acal_f$ for the set of roots of~$f(X)$, then Property~(iii) of Proposition~\ref{prop:wkmodm} can be succintly written as \begin{equation} \Delta(\Acal_f,m,n) \ge \frac{n-1}{n}. \end{equation} In particular, if $f$ satisfies the congruence \[ f(X) \equiv \F_D(X) \pmod{m} \] as in the statement of Theorem~\ref{thm:lehmodm}, then \[ \Delta(\Acal_f,m,D+1) \ge \frac{D}{D+1}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Property (iii) of the proposition is exactly $\D(\Acal_f,m,n)\ge(n-1)/n$; the classical congruence gives $\D(\Acal_f,m,D+1)\ge D/(D+1)$.
nodes.section: 1 A Reformulation of Property

nodes.name: Height lower bound in terms of $\D(\Acal,m,n)$
nodes.statement: Let $\Acal\subset\bar\QQ$ be a finite set of algebraic integers, that does not contain any roots of unity and let~$m$ and~$n$ be positive integers. Then for all integers $J\ge1$ we have \begin{equation} \sum_{\a\in\Acal}h(\a) \ge \frac{3}{J+2}\left( \D(\Acal,m,n) \log m - \frac{|\Acal|}{n}\frac{\log(J/2+1)+1}{J}\right). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: For any finite set of algebraic integers containing no root of unity, $\sum h(\a)\ge\frac{3}{J+2}(\D(\Acal,m,n)\log m-\frac{|\Acal|}{n}\frac{\log(J/2+1)+1}{J})$ for every $J\ge1$.
nodes.section: 2 A Height Bound for Polynomials Satisfying Congruence Conditions
assumptions: Let $\Acal\subset\bar\QQ$ be a finite set of algebraic integers, that does not contain any roots of unity
let~$m$ and~$n$ be positive integers
for all integers $J\ge1$
conclusions: \sum_{\a\in\Acal}h(\a) \ge \frac{3}{J+2}\left( \D(\Acal,m,n) \log m - \frac{|\Acal|}{n}\frac{\log(J/2+1)+1}{J}\right). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Choosing $J$ to make the bound nontrivial
nodes.statement: It is always possible to choose a value of~$J$ to obtain a nontrivial, i.e., positive, lower bound in~\eqref{eqn:sumhageDAmnlogm}. The optimal choice of~$J$ depends on the relative sizes of $\D(\Acal,m,n)\log m$ and $|\Acal|/n$. In the application most closely related to Theorem~\ref{thm:lehmodm}, we have \[ n=D+1\qquad\text{and}\qquad \D(\Acal,m,n)\log m = \frac{|\Acal|}{n} = \frac{D}{D+1}, \] so we get \[ \sum_{f(\a)=0} h(\a) \ge \frac{D}{D+1}\cdot\frac{3}{J+2} \cdot\left(\log m - \frac{\log(J/2+1)+1}{J}\right). \] If $m\ge5$, then we obtain a nontrivial lower bound with $J=1$, while for~$3\le m\le 4$ we need to take $J=2$, and for~$m=2$ we must take~$J=3$. Of course, the bound that we obtain is not sharp. However, our goal is not to get sharp bounds in this particular case, where other authors~\cite{BoDoMo,BoHaMo,DuMo,GaIsMoPiWi} have used intricate techniques to obtain better bounds than we could obtain even if we took more care. Instead, we aim to show how to obtain nontrivial bounds that, among other things, imply that Lehmer's conjecture is true for an interesting class of polynomials that is larger than the class considered in~\cite{BoDoMo,BoHaMo,DuMo,GaIsMoPiWi}.
nodes.statement_short: A suitable $J$ always makes the bound positive ($J=1$ for $m\ge5$, $J=2$ for $3\le m\le4$, $J=3$ for $m=2$), though the constants are not sharp.

nodes.name: Fejér kernel estimate
nodes.statement: For all $J\ge1$ we have \[ \sup_{\substack{z\in\CC\\ |z|\le 1\\}} \sum_{j=1}^J \left(1-\frac{j}{J+1}\right)\log|1-z^j| \le \frac{1}{2}\log\left(\frac{J}{2}+1\right)+\frac{1}{2}. \]
nodes.statement_short: The Fej\'er-weighted sum $\sum_j(1-\frac{j}{J+1})\log|1-z^j|$ is at most $\frac12\log(\frac J2+1)+\frac12$ on the closed unit disk.

conclusions: \sup_{\substack{z\in\CC\\ |z|\le 1\\}} \sum_{j=1}^J \left(1-\frac{j}{J+1}\right)\log|1-z^j| \le \frac{1}{2}\log\left(\frac{J}{2}+1\right)+\frac{1}{2}. \]

nodes.name: Proof of the height lower bound in terms of $\D(\Acal,m,n)$
nodes.statement_short: Fej\'er averaging: bound $(n\log m)\D$ by heights plus archimedean terms, apply it to $\Acal^j$, average with the multiplier $1-j/(J+1)$, and insert the Fej\'er kernel estimate.

nodes.name: Lehmer's conjecture for polynomials divisible by $\F_{n-1}(X)$ in $(\ZZ/m\ZZ)[X]$
nodes.statement: Fix $0<\e\le 1$. Then Lehmer's conjecture~\eqref{eqn:lehmerconj} is true for the set of polynomials \begin{equation} \left\{ f(X)\in \ZZ[X] : \begin{tabular}{@{}l@{}} $f(X)$ is monic, its roots are not roots\\ of unity, and there exist integers $m\ge2$ \\ and $n\ge\max\{2,\e\deg(f)\}$ such that\\ $\F_{n-1}(X)$ divides $f(X)$ in $(\ZZ/m\ZZ)[X]$\\ \end{tabular} \right\}. \end{equation} More precisely, if~$f(X)$ is in the set~\eqref{eqn:monicmnedegf}, then \begin{equation} \sum_{f(\a)=0} h(\a) \ge \frac{\log m}{185\e^{-1}\log(24\e^{-1})}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: For fixed $0<\e\le1$ Lehmer's conjecture holds, with explicit constant $\log m/(185\e^{-1}\log(24\e^{-1}))$, on the stated class of polynomials.

assumptions: Fix $0<\e\le 1$.
conclusions: Then Lehmer's conjecture~\eqref{eqn:lehmerconj} is true for the set of polynomials \begin{equation} \left\{ f(X)\in \ZZ[X] : \begin{tabular}{@{}l@{}} $f(X)$ is monic, its roots are not roots\\ of unity, and there exist integers $m\ge2$ \\ and $n\ge\max\{2,\e\deg(f)\}$ such that\\ $\F_{n-1}(X)$ divides $f(X)$ in $(\ZZ/m\ZZ)[X]$\\ \end{tabular} \right\}. \end{equation}
More precisely, if~$f(X)$ is in the set~\eqref{eqn:monicmnedegf}, then \begin{equation} \sum_{f(\a)=0} h(\a) \ge \frac{\log m}{185\e^{-1}\log(24\e^{-1})}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Shparlinski's observation for large $m$
nodes.statement: Igor Shparlinski has pointed out that for large~$m$, we may take $\e=(\log\log m)/(\log m)$ and conclude that if $\F_{n-1}(X)$ divides $f(X)$ in $(\ZZ/m\ZZ)[X]$ for some $n\ge((\log\log{m})/(\log{m}))(\deg{f})$, then \[ \sum_{f(\a)=0} h(\a) \ge \frac{1}{185}+ O\left(\frac{\log\log\log m}{\log\log m}\right), \] where the big-$O$ constant is absolute.
nodes.statement_short: Taking $\e=(\log\log m)/(\log m)$ gives $\sum h(\a)\ge\frac1{185}+O(\log\log\log m/\log\log m)$ with absolute implied constant.

nodes.name: Two-case explicit height bound under mod $m$ divisibility
nodes.statement: Let $f(X)\in\ZZ[X]$ be a monic polynomial of degree~$D$ whose roots are not roots of unity, let $m,n\ge2$ be integers, and suppose that~$\F_{n-1}(X)$ divides $f(X)$ in $(\ZZ/m\ZZ)[X]$. Then \[ \sum_{f(\a)=0}h(\a) \ge \begin{cases} (\log m)/264 &\text{if $\log m\ge D/16n$,} \\[1\jot] \dfrac{\log m}{(128D/n\log m)\log(16D/n\log m)} &\text{if $\log m\le D/16n$.} \\ \end{cases} \]
nodes.statement_short: Under the divisibility hypothesis, $\sum h(\a)\ge(\log m)/264$ when $\log m\ge D/16n$, and a $(128D/n\log m)\log(16D/n\log m)$-type bound otherwise.
nodes.section: 2 A Height Bound for Polynomials Satisfying Congruence Conditions
assumptions: Let $f(X)\in\ZZ[X]$ be a monic polynomial of degree~$D$ whose roots are not roots of unity,
let $m,n\ge2$ be integers,
suppose that~$\F_{n-1}(X)$ divides $f(X)$ in $(\ZZ/m\ZZ)[X]$.
conclusions: \sum_{f(\a)=0}h(\a) \ge \begin{cases} (\log m)/264 &\text{if $\log m\ge D/16n$,} \\[1\jot] \dfrac{\log m}{(128D/n\log m)\log(16D/n\log m)} &\text{if $\log m\le D/16n$.} \\ \end{cases} \]

nodes.name: Proof of the two-case explicit height bound
nodes.statement: Let~$\Acal_f$ be the set of roots of~$f$. As noted in Remark~\ref{remark:DAfmD1geDD1}, the divisibility condition on~$f$ implies that $\D(\Acal_f,m,n)\ge (n-1)/n$. Substituting this into~\eqref{eqn:sumhageDAmnlogm} of Theorem~\ref{thm:hageCDAmnlogm} and using~$|\Acal_f|=D$, we find that for all integers $J\ge1$ we have \begin{align*} \sum_{f(\a)=0}h(\a) &\ge \frac{3}{J+2} \left(\frac{n-1}{n}\log m - \frac{D}{n}\frac{\log(J/2+1)+1}{J}\right). \end{align*} Since we are not concerned with optimizing our constants, we observe that for $n\ge2$ and $J\ge2$, this implies that \begin{equation} \sum_{f(\a)=0}h(\a) \ge \frac{1}{J} \left(\frac{1}{2}\log m - \frac{4D}{n}\frac{\log(J)}{J}\right). \end{equation} We now consider two cases. First, if~$m$ is large, say \[ \log m \ge D/16n, \] then taking~$J=57$ gives \begin{equation} \sum_{f(\a)=0}h(\a) \ge \frac{1}{J}\left(\frac12-4\frac{\log(J)}{J}\right)\log m \ge \frac{\log m}{264}. \end{equation} Second, suppose that~$m$ is small, \[ \log m \le D/16n. \] Then we want to choose~$J$ to be an integer satisfying \begin{equation} \frac{J}{\log J} \ge \frac{16D}{n\log m}. \end{equation} In particular, since $16D/n\log m\ge256$, it suffices to take \[ J = \left\lfloor \frac{32D}{n\log m}\log\left(\frac{16D}{n\log m}\right) \right\rfloor - 1. \] Substituting~\eqref{eqn:JlogJge16dnlogm} into~\eqref{eqn:1J12m4DnlogJJ} and adjusting the constants yields \begin{equation} \sum_{f(\a)=0}h(\a) \ge \frac{\log m}{4J} \ge \frac{\log m}{(128D/n\log m)\log(16D/n\log m)}. \end{equation} Combining~\eqref{eqn:bd1} and~\eqref{eqn:bd2} completes the proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:htgeelogm}.
nodes.statement_short: Substitute $\D(\Acal_f,m,n)\ge(n-1)/n$ into the main theorem, weaken constants, then split into the cases $\log m\ge D/16n$ ($J=57$) and $\log m\le D/16n$ (explicit $J$).
nodes.section: 2 A Height Bound for Polynomials Satisfying Congruence Conditions

nodes.name: Proof of Lehmer's conjecture for the stated class of polynomials
nodes.statement: We are given that $n\ge\max\{\e D,2\}$. If $\log m\ge D/16n$, then Lemma~\ref{lemma:htgeelogm} says that \[ \sum_{f(\a)=0}h(\a) \ge \frac{\log m}{264}. \] This is stronger than~\eqref{eqn:logm185e}, since we have assumed that $\e\le1$, so we are reduced to the case that~$\log m\le D/16n$. Since $n\ge\e D$, this implies that \[ \frac{D}{n\log m}\le\frac{D}{\e D\log m} \le \frac{1}{\e\log m}, \] where the upper bound is at least~$16$. Substituting this into Lemma~\ref{lemma:htgeelogm}, we find that \[ \sum_{f(\a)=0}h(\a) \ge \frac{\log m}{(128/\e\log m)\log(16/\e\log m)}. \] Since~$m\ge2$, this gives something slightly stronger than the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Handle $\log m\ge D/16n$ by the lemma directly, then use $n\ge\e D$ to bound $D/(n\log m)$ in the remaining case.

nodes.name: Canonical height and local canonical height on an elliptic curve
nodes.statement: Let~$E/K$ be an elliptic curve defined over a number field. We write \[ \hhat : E(\Kbar)\longrightarrow \RR \] for the absolute logarithmic canonical height~\cite[VIII~\S9]{MR2514094}, and for each~$v\in M_\Kbar$ we let \[ \lhat_v : E(\Kbar_v)\setminus\{O\}\longrightarrow\RR \] be a local canonical height, normalized as described in~\cite[Chapter~VI]{ATAEC}.
nodes.statement_short: Fixes $\hhat:E(\Kbar)\to\RR$ as the absolute logarithmic canonical height and $\lhat_v$ as the normalized local canonical height at $v$.
nodes.section: 3 An Elliptic Analogue of $\D(\Acal,m,n)$
nodes.origin_citation: Silverman, The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves VIII§9; Silverman, ATAEC Chapter VI

nodes.name: Properties of the local canonical height
nodes.statement: The local canonical height satisfies the following\textup: \begin{parts} \Part{(a)} For all $v\in M_K$ there is a constant $c(v)$ such that \[ \l_v(P)\ge -c(v)\quad\text{for all $P\in E(\Kbar_v)$.} \] Further, if~$v\in M_K^0$ and~$E$ has good reduction at~$v$, then we can take~$c(v)=0$. \Part{(b)} The global height is the sum of the local heights. Thus for any finite extension $L/K$ and any $P\in E(L)\setminus\{O\}$ we have \[ \hhat(P) = \sum_{v\in M_L} \lhat_v(P). \] \end{parts}
nodes.statement_short: Local heights are bounded below (and non-negative at good-reduction nonarchimedean places), and the global canonical height is the sum of the local ones.
nodes.section: 3 An Elliptic Analogue of $\D(\Acal,m,n)$
nodes.origin_citation: Silverman, ATAEC, Theorems VI.1.1, VI.4.1, VI.2.1
conclusions: \Part{(a)} For all $v\in M_K$ there is a constant $c(v)$ such that \[ \l_v(P)\ge -c(v)\quad\text{for all $P\in E(\Kbar_v)$.} \] Further, if~$v\in M_K^0$ and~$E$ has good reduction at~$v$, then we can take~$c(v)=0$.
\Part{(b)} The global height is the sum of the local heights. Thus for any finite extension $L/K$ and any $P\in E(L)\setminus\{O\}$ we have \[ \hhat(P) = \sum_{v\in M_L} \lhat_v(P). \]

nodes.name: Proof of the properties of the local canonical height
nodes.statement: The first part of~(a) follows from~\cite[Theorem~VI.1.1(a)]{ATAEC}, which says in particular that~$\lhat_v$ has a logarithmic pole as $P\to O$ in the $v$-adic topology and that~$\l_v$ is bounded on the complement of any $v$-adic neighborhood of~$O$. The second part of~(a) follow from~\cite[Theorem~VI.4.1]{ATAEC}, which says that if~$P$ reduces to a non-singular point modulo~$v$, then \[ \lhat_v(P) = \frac12\max\bigl\{-v\bigl(x(P)\bigr),0\bigr\} +\frac1{12}v(\gD_{E/K}). \] This quantity is clearly non-negative. Finally, \cite[Theorem~VI.2.1]{ATAEC} gives a proof of~(b).
nodes.statement_short: Quote the pole/boundedness statement, the explicit good-reduction formula, and the sum-of-local-heights theorem from ATAEC.

nodes.origin_citation: Silverman, ATAEC, Theorems VI.1.1, VI.4.1, VI.2.1

nodes.name: Elliptic analogue $\D(\Pcal,\gm,n)$
nodes.statement: Given \begin{itemize} \item[$K/\QQ$] a number field, \item[$\gm$] an integral idea of $K$ with norm $m=\Norm_{K/\QQ}\gm\ge2$, \item[$E/K$] an elliptic curve, and \item[$\Pcal$] a finite set of nontorsion points in $E(\Kbar)$, \end{itemize} we define \[ \Delta(\Pcal,\gm,n) = \sum_{P\in\Pcal} \frac{1}{\log m}\sum_{v\mid\gm} \frac{1}{n^2} \lhat_v(nP). \] This quantity is the elliptic analogue of the quantity~$\D(\Acal,m,n)$ that we defined in Section~\ref{section:prop1}.
nodes.statement_short: $\D(\Pcal,\gm,n)=\sum_{P\in\Pcal}\frac1{\log m}\sum_{v\mid\gm}\frac1{n^2}\lhat_v(nP)$, the elliptic counterpart of $\D(\Acal,m,n)$.
nodes.section: 3 An Elliptic Analogue of $\D(\Acal,m,n)$

nodes.name: Monotonicity of the elliptic $\D$ under multiplication by $j$
nodes.statement: With notation as above, assume that~$E$ has potential good reduction at every prime dividing~$\gm$. Let $j\ge1$ be an integer, and let $j\Pcal=\{jP:P\in\Pcal\}$. Then \[ \Delta(j\Pcal,\gm,n)\ge \Delta(\Pcal,\gm, n). \]
nodes.statement_short: Under potential good reduction at the primes dividing $\gm$, $\D(j\Pcal,\gm,n)\ge\D(\Pcal,\gm,n)$.
nodes.section: 3 An Elliptic Analogue of $\D(\Acal,m,n)$
assumptions: With notation as above, assume that~$E$ has potential good reduction at every prime dividing~$\gm$.
Let $j\ge1$ be an integer, and let $j\Pcal=\{jP:P\in\Pcal\}$.
conclusions: \Delta(j\Pcal,\gm,n)\ge \Delta(\Pcal,\gm, n).

nodes.name: Proof of monotonicity of the elliptic $\D$
nodes.statement: Replacing~$K$ by a finite extension, we may assume that~$E$ has good reduction at all primes dividing~$\gm$. Let~$v\in M_K^0$ be any place at which~$E$ has good reduction, and let~$\pi_v\in K$ be a uniformizer at~$v$. Further, let \[ E_0(\Kbar_v) \subset E_1(\Kbar_v) \subset E_2(\Kbar_v) \subset \cdots \] be the formal group filtration of~$E(\Kbar_v)$; see~\cite[Chapters~IV,~VII]{MR2514094}. Here $E_0=E$, since we have assumed good reduction, and~$E_1$ is the formal group. The explicit formula for~$\lhat_v$~\cite[Theorem~VI.4.1]{ATAEC} then has the form \[ \lhat_v(P) = \max\bigl\{r\ge0 : P \in E_r(\Kbar_v)\bigr\}v(\pi_v). \] Since the filtration consists of subgroups, it is immediate that \[ \lhat_v(jP) \ge \lhat_v(P) \qquad\text{for all $j\ge1$.} \] Summing over $P\in\Pcal$ and $v\mid\gm$, and dividing by $n^2\log m$, the desired result is immediate from the definition of~$\D$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to good reduction, use the formal-group-filtration formula for $\lhat_v$, and note that filtration levels can only increase under multiplication by $j$.

nodes.name: Explicit formula for the local canonical height via the formal group filtration
nodes.statement: \lhat_v(P) = \max\bigl\{r\ge0 : P \in E_r(\Kbar_v)\bigr\}v(\pi_v).

nodes.name: Failure of monotonicity at potential multiplicative reduction
nodes.statement: If~$E$ has potential multiplicative reduction at~$v$, then it is possible to have $\lhat_v(jP)<\lhat_v(P)$, so~$\D(j\Pcal,\gm,n)$ may be strictly smaller than~$\D(\Pcal,\gm,n)$.
nodes.statement_short: At potential multiplicative reduction one can have $\lhat_v(jP)<\lhat_v(P)$, so $\D(j\Pcal,\gm,n)$ may be strictly smaller than $\D(\Pcal,\gm,n)$.

nodes.name: $M_K$-constant and normalized $M_\Qbar$-constant
nodes.statement: Let $K/\QQ$ be a number field. An \emph{$M_K$-constant} is a map \[ c : M_K\longrightarrow [0,\infty) \] with the property that $\{v\in M_K:c(v)\ne0\}$ is a finite set. (For convenience, we consider only non-negative $M_K$-constants.) A \emph{normalized} \emph{$M_\Qbar$-constant} is a collection of $M_K$-constants \[ c_K : M_K\longrightarrow\RR, \] one for each number field~$K/\QQ$, satisfying the compatibility condition that for all number fields $L/K$ and all~$v\in M_K$, \[ \sum_{w\in M_L,\, w|v} \frac{[L_w:K_v]}{[L:K]}c_L(w) = c_K(v). \]
nodes.statement_short: An $M_K$-constant is a non-negative function on $M_K$ vanishing off a finite set; a normalized $M_\Qbar$-constant is a compatible family of these over all number fields.
nodes.section: 4 A Height Lower Bound for Points on Elliptic Curves
differentia: with the property that $\{v\in M_K:c(v)\ne0\}$ is a finite set.

nodes.name: Fourier averaging estimate for local canonical heights
nodes.statement: Let $E/\Qbar$ be an elliptic curve. There are normalized $M_{\Qbar}$-constants $c_1$ and~$c_2$, depending only on~$E$, such that for all integers~$J\ge2$, all nontorsion points~$P\in E(\Qbar)$, and all absolute values~$v\in M_\Qbar$ we have \begin{equation} \sum_{j=1}^J \left(1-\frac{j}{J+1}\right)\lhat_v(jP) \ge -c_1(v)\log(J)-c_2(v). \end{equation} \textup(We may, in fact, take $c_1(v)=0$ for all nonarchimedean~$v$.\textup)
nodes.statement_short: There are $M_\Qbar$-constants $c_1,c_2$ with $\sum_{j=1}^J(1-\frac{j}{J+1})\lhat_v(jP)\ge -c_1(v)\log J-c_2(v)$ for all nontorsion $P$ and all $v$.
nodes.section: 4 A Height Lower Bound for Points on Elliptic Curves
nodes.origin_citation: Hindry & Silverman 1988, 1990; Elkies, in Lang, Introduction to Arakelov Theory, Theorem 5.1
assumptions: Let $E/\Qbar$ be an elliptic curve.
conclusions: There are normalized $M_{\Qbar}$-constants $c_1$ and~$c_2$, depending only on~$E$, such that for all integers~$J\ge2$, all nontorsion points~$P\in E(\Qbar)$, and all absolute values~$v\in M_\Qbar$ we have \begin{equation} \sum_{j=1}^J \left(1-\frac{j}{J+1}\right)\lhat_v(jP) \ge -c_1(v)\log(J)-c_2(v). \end{equation}
\textup(We may, in fact, take $c_1(v)=0$ for all nonarchimedean~$v$.\textup)

nodes.name: Proof of the Fourier averaging estimate
nodes.statement: If~$v$ is nonarchimedean and~$E$ has good reduction at~$v$, then the local height~$\lhat_v$ is non-negative, so we can take $c_1(v)=c_2(v)=0$. For nonarchimedean~$v$ of bad reduction, the inequality~\eqref{eqn:fejarjPgec1v} with $c_1(v)=0$ is proven in~\cite{HiSi2}. Finally, for archimedean~$v$, the local height functions are Green's functions and the desired result follows from a general theorem of Elkies~\cite[Theorem~5.1]{LangAT} that is valid on curves of positive genus. More precisely, Elkies' theorem says that there is a constant $c=c(E,v)$ such that for any distinct points~$P_0,\ldots,P_J\in E(K_v)$ we have \begin{equation} \sum_{0\le i<j\le J} \lhat_v(P_j-P_i) \ge -\frac{1}{2\pi}(J+1)\log J - cJ. \end{equation} (We are using the fact that~$\lhat_v$ is an even function.) Taking $P_j=jP$ for $0\le j\le J$, we find that \begin{equation} \sum_{0\le i<j\le J} \lhat_v(P_j-P_i) = \sum_{0\le i<j\le J} \lhat_v\bigl((j-i)P\bigr) = \sum_{j=1}^J (J+1-j)\lhat_v(jP). \end{equation} Combining~\eqref{eqn1} and~\eqref{eqn2} and dividing by~$J+1$ gives~\eqref{eqn:fejarjPgec1v}.
nodes.statement_short: Case analysis over places: trivial at good nonarchimedean places, quoted from Hindry-Silverman at bad ones, and derived from Elkies' Green's-function theorem at archimedean ones.

nodes.name: Height lower bound for points in terms of $\D(\Pcal,\gm,n)$
nodes.statement: Suppose that we are given the following quantities\textup: \begin{notation} \item[$K/\QQ$] a number field. \item[$E/K$] an elliptic curve. \item[$n$] a positive integer. \item[$\gm$] an integral ideal of~$K$ with norm $m=\Norm_{K/\QQ}\gm\ge2$. \item[$\Pcal$] a finite set of nontorsion points in $E(\Kbar)$. \end{notation} Suppose further that~$E$ has potential good reduction at every prime dividing~$\gm$. Then there is a constant $C_E$, depending only on~$E$, such that for all integers~$J\ge1$ we have \[ \sum_{P\in\Pcal} \hhat(P) \ge \frac{6}{(J+1)(J+2)}\left(\D(\Pcal,\gm,n)\log m -C_E \frac{|\Pcal|}{n^2}\cdot\frac{\log(J+1)}{J}\right). \]
nodes.statement_short: Under potential good reduction at $\gm$, $\sum_{P\in\Pcal}\hhat(P)\ge\frac{6}{(J+1)(J+2)}(\D(\Pcal,\gm,n)\log m-C_E\frac{|\Pcal|}{n^2}\frac{\log(J+1)}{J})$.

assumptions: Suppose that we are given the following quantities\textup: \begin{notation} \item[$K/\QQ$] a number field. \item[$E/K$] an elliptic curve. \item[$n$] a positive integer. \item[$\gm$] an integral ideal of~$K$ with norm $m=\Norm_{K/\QQ}\gm\ge2$. \item[$\Pcal$] a finite set of nontorsion points in $E(\Kbar)$. \end{notation}
Suppose further that~$E$ has potential good reduction at every prime dividing~$\gm$.

nodes.name: Proof of the elliptic height lower bound
nodes.statement: To ease notation, we let \[ f_j = 1-\frac{j}{J+1} \qquad\text{and}\qquad F_k = \sum_{j=1}^J j^kf_j. \] Earlier we used the values of~$F_0$ and~$F_1$. In this section we will use the values \begin{equation} F_0 = \frac{J}{2} \qquad\text{and}\qquad F_2 = \frac{J(J+1)(J+2)}{12}. \end{equation} \par Replacing~$K$ by a finite extension, we may assume that~$\Pcal\subset E(K)$. We let \[ M_K^\bad = M_K^\infty \cup \{v\in M_K^0 : \text{$E$ has bad reduction at $v$}\} . \] Then \[ v\in M_K\setminus M_K^\bad \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \l_v(Q)\ge0\quad\text{for all $Q\in E(\Kbar_v)$.} \] \par We compute \begin{align*} n^2\sum_{P\in\Pcal} \hhat(P) & = \sum_{P\in\Pcal} \hhat(nP) \\ & = \sum_{P\in\Pcal} \sum_{v\in M_K} \lhat_v(nP) \\ &\ge \sum_{P\in\Pcal} \sum_{v\mid\gm} \lhat_v(nP) + \sum_{P\in\Pcal} \sum_{v\in M_K^\bad} \lhat_v(nP) \\ &= (n^2\log m)\D(\Pcal,\gm,n) + \sum_{P\in\Pcal} \sum_{v\in M_K^\bad} \lhat_v(nP). \end{align*} Replacing~$\Pcal$ with $j\Pcal=\{jP:P\in\Pcal\}$ and using Lemma~\ref{lemma:DjPgeDP}, which says that $\D(j\Pcal,\gm,n)\ge\D(\Pcal,\gm,n)$ (this is where we use the assumption that~$E$ has potential good reduction at the primes dividing~$\gm$), we find that \[ n^2j^2\sum_{P\in\Pcal} \hhat(P) \ge (n^2\log m)\D(\Pcal,\gm,n) + \sum_{P\in\Pcal} \sum_{v\in M_K^\bad} \lhat_v(njP). \] Multiplying both sides by~$f_j$ and summing $j=1$ to~$J$ gives \begin{align*} F_2n^2\sum_{P\in\Pcal}& \hhat(P)\\ &\ge F_0(n^2\log m)\D(\Pcal,\gm,n) + \sum_{j=1}^J \sum_{P\in\Pcal} \sum_{v\in M_K^\bad} f_j\lhat_v(njP) \\ &\ge F_0(n^2\log m)\D(\Pcal,\gm,n) + |\Pcal|\sum_{v\in M_K^\bad} \inf_{Q\in E(K)} \sum_{j=1}^J f_j\lhat_v(jQ). \end{align*} Proposition~\ref{prop:fourieravg} says that there are~$M_K$-constants~$c_1$ and~$c_2$, depending only on~$E$, such that \[ \inf_{Q\in E(K)} \sum_{j=1}^J f_j\lhat_v(jQ) \ge -c_1(v)\log(J)-c_2(v). \] Summing over $v\in M_K^\bad$ gives constants that depend only on~$E$, so adjusting the constants and using the assumption that $J\ge1$, we find that there is a constant~$C_E$, depending only on~$E$, such that \[ F_2n^2\sum_{P\in\Pcal} \hhat(P) \ge F_0(n^2\log m)\D(\Pcal,\gm,n) -C_E |\Pcal|\log(J+1). \] Using the formulas~\eqref{eqn:F0F1F2} for~$F_0$ and~$F_2$, dividing by~$F_2n^2$, and adjusting the constant gives the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Fej\'er averaging on elliptic local heights: decompose $\hhat(nP)$ into local heights, replace $\Pcal$ by $j\Pcal$, average against $f_j$, and control the bad places by the Fourier averaging estimate.
nodes.section: 4 A Height Lower Bound for Points on Elliptic Curves

nodes.name: The conjugate set $\Pcal_Q$ and the degree $D_Q$
nodes.statement: Let $E/K$ be an elliptic curve and let $Q\in E(\Kbar)$. We let \[ \Pcal_Q = \{\s(Q) : \s\in\Gal(\Kbar/K)\} \quad\text{and}\quad D_Q = [K(Q):K] = |\Pcal_Q|. \] We remark that all of the points in~$\Pcal_Q$ have the same canonical height; cf.~\cite[Theorem~VIII.5.10]{MR2514094}.
nodes.statement_short: $\Pcal_Q$ is the Galois orbit of $Q$ and $D_Q=[K(Q):K]=|\Pcal_Q|$; all points of $\Pcal_Q$ share the same canonical height.
nodes.section: 4 A Height Lower Bound for Points on Elliptic Curves

nodes.name: Elliptic Lehmer conjecture for points with $\D(\Pcal_Q,\gm,n)\ge\d$
nodes.statement: Let~$E/K$ be an elliptic curve defined over a number field. Fix constants $\d,\e>0$. Then the elliptic Lehmer conjecture~\eqref{eqn:ellipticlehmer} is true for the following set of points\textup: \begin{equation} \left\{ Q \in E(\Kbar) : \parbox{.65\hsize}{\noindent there exists an integral ideal $\gm$ of $K$ with $\Norm_{K/\QQ}\gm\ge2$ such that $E$ has good reduction at all primes dividing $\gm$ and an integer $n\ge\max\{\sqrt{\e D_Q},2\}$ with $\D(\Pcal_Q,\gm,n)\ge\d$ } \right\}. \end{equation} For points in the set~\eqref{eqn:QEKbarDd}, the constant in~\eqref{eqn:ellipticlehmer} will have the form $C_{E/K,\d,\e}\log{m}$, where $C_{E/K,\d,\e}$ is positive and depends only on the indicated quantities.
nodes.statement_short: The elliptic Lehmer conjecture holds, with constant $C_{E/K,\d,\e}\log m$, for points admitting an ideal $\gm$ of good reduction and $n\ge\max\{\sqrt{\e D_Q},2\}$ with $\D(\Pcal_Q,\gm,n)\ge\d$.
nodes.section: 4 A Height Lower Bound for Points on Elliptic Curves
assumptions: Let~$E/K$ be an elliptic curve defined over a number field.
Fix constants $\d,\e>0$.
conclusions: Then the elliptic Lehmer conjecture~\eqref{eqn:ellipticlehmer} is true for the following set of points\textup: \begin{equation} \left\{ Q \in E(\Kbar) : \parbox{.65\hsize}{\noindent there exists an integral ideal $\gm$ of $K$ with $\Norm_{K/\QQ}\gm\ge2$ such that $E$ has good reduction at all primes dividing $\gm$ and an integer $n\ge\max\{\sqrt{\e D_Q},2\}$ with $\D(\Pcal_Q,\gm,n)\ge\d$ } \right\}. \end{equation}

For points in the set~\eqref{eqn:QEKbarDd}, the constant in~\eqref{eqn:ellipticlehmer} will have the form $C_{E/K,\d,\e}\log{m}$, where $C_{E/K,\d,\e}$ is positive and depends only on the indicated quantities.

nodes.name: Proof of the elliptic Lehmer conjecture for the stated set of points
nodes.statement: We are given that $n\ge\sqrt{\e D_Q}$ and $\D(\Pcal_Q,\gm,n)\ge\d$. Using these values in Theorem~\ref{thm:sumhhatPgeD} together with some trivial estimates yields \[ \sum_{P\in\Pcal_Q}\hhat(P) \ge \frac{1}{J^2}\left(\d\log m -\frac{C_E}{\e}\cdot\frac{\log(J+1)}{J}\right). \] We now choose~$J$ to be the smallest integer satisfying \[ \frac{\log(J+1)}{J} \le \min\left\{ \frac{\e\d}{2C_E}\log m, \frac12\right\}. \] This yields an estimate of the desired form \[ D_Q\hhat(Q) \ge C_{E/K,\d,\e}\log m, \] where we are using the fact, noted earlier, that every point in~$\Pcal_Q$ has canonical height equal to~$\hhat(Q)$.
nodes.statement_short: Insert $n\ge\sqrt{\e D_Q}$ and $\D\ge\d$ into the elliptic height bound and choose $J$ minimal with $\log(J+1)/J$ small enough.
nodes.section: 4 A Height Lower Bound for Points on Elliptic Curves

nodes.name: Length of a polynomial
nodes.statement: The \emph{length} of a polynomial $g(X)=\sum a_iX^i\in\ZZ[X]$ is the quantity \[ L(g) = \sum |a_i|. \]
nodes.section: 5 Other Congruence Conditions on the Coefficients

nodes.name: Height bound for other congruence conditions (special case of Samuels)
nodes.statement: \textup{(Special Case of \cite[Corollary~5.3]{MR2313990})} Let $m\ge2$ and let~$f(X)\in\ZZ[X]$ be a monic polynomial of degree~$D$ satisfying $f(1)\ne0$. Further let $u(X)\in\ZZ[X]$ be a polynomial of degree at most~$D-1$, and suppose that \[ f(X)\equiv \F_D(X) + u(X) \pmod{m}, \] but that~$f(X)$ has no roots in common with $\F_D(X)+u(X)$. Then \begin{align*} \sum_{f(\a)=0} h(\a) &\ge \frac{D}{D+1} \log\left(\frac{m}{L\bigl(X^{D+1}-1+(X-1)u(X)\bigr)}\right). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: If $f\equiv\F_D+u\pmod m$ with no common roots, then $\sum h(\a)\ge\frac{D}{D+1}\log\frac{m}{L(X^{D+1}-1+(X-1)u(X))}$.
nodes.section: 5 Other Congruence Conditions on the Coefficients
assumptions: Let $m\ge2$ and let~$f(X)\in\ZZ[X]$ be a monic polynomial of degree~$D$ satisfying $f(1)\ne0$.
Further let $u(X)\in\ZZ[X]$ be a polynomial of degree at most~$D-1$, and suppose that \[ f(X)\equiv \F_D(X) + u(X) \pmod{m}, \]
but that~$f(X)$ has no roots in common with $\F_D(X)+u(X)$.
conclusions: \sum_{f(\a)=0} h(\a) &\ge \frac{D}{D+1} \log\left(\frac{m}{L\bigl(X^{D+1}-1+(X-1)u(X)\bigr)}\right). \end{align*}

nodes.statement:
We are given that \[ f(X) = \F_D(X) + u(X) + mr(X) \qquad	ext{for some $r(X)\in\ZZ[X]$.} \] Then  egin{align*} \Resultant igl(f(X)&,X^{D+1}-1+(X-1)u(X) igr)\* &= \Resultant igl(f(X),\F_D(X)+u(X) igr) \cdot\Resultant igl(f(X),X-1 igr) \ &= \Resultant igl(mr(X),\F_D(X)+u(X) igr)f(1) \ &= m^D\Resultant igl(r(X),\F_D(X)+u(X) igr)f(1). \end{align*} By assumption, the resultants are nonzero integers, so we find that  egin{align} D\log m &\le \log\left|\Resultant igl(f(X),X^{D+1}-1+(X-1)u(X) igr)ight| 
otag\ &= \sum_{f(\a)=0} \sum_{v\in M_K^\infty} \log\|\a^{D+1}-1+(\a-1)u(\a)\|_v 
otag\ &= \sum_{v\in M_K^\infty}\sum_{\substack{f(\a)=0\\|\a\|_v>1\}} \log\|\a^{D+1}\|_v 
otag\ &\qquad{} + \sum_{v\in M_K^\infty}\sum_{\substack{f(\a)=0\\|\a\|_v>1\}} \log\left\| rac{\a^{D+1}-1+(\a-1)u(\a)}{\a^{D+1}}ight\|_v 
otag\ &\qquad{} + \sum_{v\in M_K^\infty}\sum_{\substack{f(\a)=0\\|\a\|_v\le1\}} \log\|\a^{D+1}-1+(\a-1)u(\a)\|_v 
otag\ &\le h(\a^{D+1}) + D\sup_{|z|=1}\log igl|z^{D+1}-1+(z-1)u(z) igr| \ &\le (D+1)h(\a) + D\log L igl(X^{D+1}-1+(X-1)u(X) igr).

nodes.statement_short: Factor $\Resultant(f,X^{D+1}-1+(X-1)u)$ to extract $m^D$, then bound $D\log m$ by archimedean contributions and the length $L$.
nodes.section: 5 Other Congruence Conditions on the Coefficients

nodes.name: Limits of the argument for general congruences
nodes.statement: The upshot of Theorem~\ref{thm:othercongruences} is that if~$m$ is sufficiently large, then we obtain a Lehmer-type lower bound. However, in the cyclotomic case, i.e., $u=0$, a Fourier averaging argument allowed us to prove nontrivial estimates for all values of~$m\ge2$. We do not know how to perform such an averaging argument in the general case. It would also be interesting to prove a version of Theorem~\ref{thm:othercongruences} under the weaker assumption that~$f(X)$ is divisible modulo~$m$ by~$\F_{n-1}(X)$ for, say, $n\ge\e D$. Again we do not have the requisite averaging lemma.
nodes.statement_short: A Lehmer-type bound follows only for large $m$; no averaging argument is known in the general (non-cyclotomic) case.
nodes.section: 5 Other Congruence Conditions on the Coefficients

nodes.name: An averaging argument for general congruence conditions
nodes.statement: We do not know how to perform such an averaging argument in the general case. It would also be interesting to prove a version of Theorem~\ref{thm:othercongruences} under the weaker assumption that~$f(X)$ is divisible modulo~$m$ by~$\F_{n-1}(X)$ for, say, $n\ge\e D$. Again we do not have the requisite averaging lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Find the averaging lemma needed to extend the non-cyclotomic congruence bound to all $m\ge2$ and to divisibility by $\F_{n-1}$ with $n\ge\e D$.
nodes.section: 5 Other Congruence Conditions on the Coefficients

nodes.name: The case $u=0$ recovers the classical form of the bound
nodes.statement: If we take $u=0$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:othercongruences}, we obtain the estimate \[ \sum_{f(\a)=0} h(\a) \ge \frac{D}{D+1}\log\frac{m}{2}. \] This has the same form as Theorem~\ref{thm:lehmodm}, although the constant in Theorem~\ref{thm:lehmodm} is a little bit better than ours (and our estimate is trivial for $m=2$). On the other hand, it is interesting that such an elementary argument produces a lower bound that agrees with the best known lower bounds~\cite{BoDoMo,BoHaMo,DuMo,GaIsMoPiWi} up to an additional~$O(1/m^2)$.
nodes.statement_short: Taking $u=0$ gives $\sum h(\a)\ge\frac{D}{D+1}\log\frac m2$, matching the best known bounds up to $O(1/m^2)$.
nodes.section: 5 Other Congruence Conditions on the Coefficients

nodes.name: The case $u(X)=-2$ and the sharpness of the length bound
nodes.statement: The estimate proven in Theorem~\ref{thm:othercongruences} is nontrivial if and only if $m>L\bigl(X^{D+1}-1+(X-1)u(X)\bigr)$. As Samuels does in~\cite{MR2313990}, it is sometimes possible to improve the estimate a little bit. We illustrate with the case $u(X)=-2$, so \[ f(X)\equiv X^D+X^{D-1}+\cdots+X^2+X-1\pmod{m} \] and \[ L\bigl(X^{D+1}-1-(X-1)u(X)\bigr) = L(X^{D+1}-2X+1)=4. \] This gives a nontrivial height bound for $m\ge5$. If~$D$ is odd, then the supremum in~\eqref{eqn:DlogmaD1DLX} occurs at~$z=-1$ and is equal to~$\log4$, but if~$D$ is even, then the supremum is strictly smaller than~$\log4$ and we can obtain a small improvement in the theorem. However, for large (even) values of~$D$ we have \[ \sup_{|z|=1} |z^{D+1}-2z+1| = 4+O(D^{-2}) \quad \text{at $z\approx -e^{\pi i/(D+1)}$,} \] so for $m=4$ we only obtain $\sum h(\a) \gg D^{-2}$, which is weaker than Lehmer's conjecture.
nodes.statement_short: For $u(X)=-2$ the length is $4$, giving a nontrivial bound for $m\ge5$; for $m=4$ one only gets $\sum h(\a)\gg D^{-2}$.
nodes.section: 5 Other Congruence Conditions on the Coefficients

nodes.name: Damping inequality for $\log|1-e^{i\theta}|$
nodes.statement: For all $\theta\in\RR\setminus2\pi i\ZZ$ and all $t\ge0$ we have \[ \log|1-e^{i\theta}| \le \log|1-e^{-t}e^{i\theta}| + \frac12t. \]
nodes.statement_short: $\log|1-e^{i\theta}|\le\log|1-e^{-t}e^{i\theta}|+\frac12t$ for all real $\theta\notin2\pi i\ZZ$ and all $t\ge0$.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Proposition
assumptions: For all $\theta\in\RR\setminus2\pi i\ZZ$ and all $t\ge0$
conclusions: \log|1-e^{i\theta}| \le \log|1-e^{-t}e^{i\theta}| + \frac12t.

nodes.name: Proof of the damping inequality
nodes.statement: For notational convenience we let \[ F_t(\theta) = \log|1-e^{-t}e^{i\theta}| + \frac12t - \log|1-e^{i\theta}|, \] so we need to prove that $F_t(\theta)\ge0$. We have \[ F_0(\theta)=0 \qquad\text{for all $\theta\in\RR\setminus2\pi i\ZZ$.} \] For $t>0$ we observe that \[ \log|1-e^{-t}e^{i\theta}| = \Re\biggl(\sum_{n=1}^\infty -\frac{e^{-nt}e^{in\theta}}{n}\biggr) \] is given by an absolutely convergent series, so we may differentiate it term-by-term. Hence \begin{align*} \frac{\partial F_t}{\partial t}(\theta) &= \Re\biggl(\sum_{n=1}^\infty (e^{-t+i\theta})^n\biggr) + \frac12 = \Re\left( \frac{e^{-t+i\theta}}{1-e^{-t+i\theta}}\right) + \frac12 \\ &= \frac{e^{2t}-1}{(e^t-\cos\theta)^2+\sin^2\theta} > 0 \qquad\text{for all $t>0$.} \end{align*} Thus for any fixed $\theta\in\RR\setminus2\pi i\ZZ$, the function~$F_t(\theta)$ as a function of~$t\ge0$ satisfies~$F_0(\theta)=0$ and~$(\partial F_t/\partial t)(\theta)\ge 0$. Hence~$F_t(\theta)\ge0$ for all $t\ge0$.
nodes.statement_short: Set $F_t(\theta)$ to be the difference, check $F_0=0$, and differentiate the log-series term-by-term to show $\partial F_t/\partial t>0$.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Proposition

nodes.name: Proof of the Fejér kernel estimate
nodes.statement: The functions $\log|1-z^j|$ are harmonic on the open unit disk $|z|<1$, so the maximum occurs on the boundary. For $z=e^{i\theta}$ on the unit circle we estimate \begin{align*} \sum_{j=1}^J&\left(1-\frac{j}{J+1}\right)\log|1-z^j|\\ &\le \sum_{j=1}^J \left(1-\frac{j}{J+1}\right) \left(\log|1-e^{-t}e^{ij\theta}| + \frac12t\right) &&\text{from Lemma \ref{lemma:Gttheta},} \\ &= \Re\biggl( \sum_{j=1}^J \left(1-\frac{j}{J+1}\right) \sum_{k=1}^\infty -\frac{e^{-kt}e^{ijk\theta}}{k} \biggr) + \frac{Jt}{4} \\ &= \Re\biggl( \sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac{e^{-kt}}{k}\sum_{j=1}^J -\left(1-\frac{j}{J+1}\right)e^{ijk\theta} \biggr)+ \frac{Jt}{4} \\ &= \sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac{e^{-kt}}{k} \biggl(\frac12 -\frac{1}{2J+2}\biggl|\sum_{j=0}^Je^{ijk\theta}\biggr|^2\biggr) + \frac{Jt}{4} \hidewidth\\ &\ge \sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac{e^{-kt}}{2k} + \frac{Jt}{4} \\ &= -\frac12\log(1-e^{-t}) + \frac{Jt}{4}. \end{align*} This estimate holds for all $t>0$, so in particular we can set $t=\log(1+2J^{-1})$, which (after some algebra) gives the estimate \[ \sum_{j=1}^J f_j\log|1-z^j| \le \frac12\log\left(\frac{J}{2}+1\right) +\frac{J}{4}\log\left(1+\frac{2}{J}\right). \] Finally we observe that $x\log(1+x^{-1})\le 1$ for all $x\ge0$, which gives the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the unit circle by harmonicity, expand with the damping lemma into a Fej\'er-kernel sum, then optimize $t=\log(1+2J^{-1})$.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Proposition

nodes.name: (i) implies (ii)
nodes.statement: Property~(i) says that \[ f(X) = \F_{n-1}(X)A(X) + mB(X) \quad\text{for some $A(X),B(X)\in\ZZ[X]$.} \] This implies that \begin{align*} \Resultant\bigl(f(X),\F_{n-1}(X)\bigr) &= \Resultant\bigl(\F_{n-1}(X)A(X) + mB(X),\F_{n-1}(X)\bigr)\\ &= \Resultant\bigl(mB(X),\F_{n-1}(X)\bigr)\\ &= m^{n-1} \Resultant\bigl(B(X),\F_{n-1}(X)\bigr). \end{align*} Thus~(ii) is true. \par
nodes.statement_short: Write $f=\F_{n-1}A+mB$ and compute the resultant to extract the factor $m^{n-1}$.
nodes.section: 1 A Reformulation of Property

nodes.name: (ii) implies (iii)
nodes.statement: We next prove that~(ii) implies~(iii). For any non-archimedean absolute value~$v$ we have \begin{align} \bigl\|\Resultant\bigl(f(X),x^{n}-1\bigr)\bigr\|_v &= \bigl\|\Resultant\bigl(f(X),\F_{n-1}(X)\bigr)\bigr\|_v \bigl\|f(1)\bigr\|_v \notag\\* &\le \|m\|_v^{n-1}. \end{align} \par A standard formula for the resultant~\cite[Section~V.10]{lang:algebra} is \begin{equation} \Resultant\bigl(f(X),X^{n}-1\bigr) = \prod_{f(\a)=0} (\a^{n}-1). \end{equation} We take the $v$-absolute value of~\eqref{eqn:resproddef}, use~\eqref{eqn:resgemD}, and multiply over all~$v\mid m$ to obtain the estimate \begin{equation} \prod_{v\mid m} \prod_{f(\a)=0} \|\a^{n}-1\|_v \le \prod_{v\mid m} \|m\|_v^{n-1} = m^{-(n-1)}. \end{equation} Taking~$-\log(\,\cdot\,)$ gives~(iii).
nodes.statement_short: Bound the $v$-adic size of the resultant, expand it as a product over the roots, and take $-\log$.
nodes.section: 1 A Reformulation of Property

nodes.name: Local inequality from the factorization of $X^{jn}-1$
nodes.statement: From the factorization \[ X^{jn}-1 = (X^n-1)\F_{j-1}(X^n), \] we see that \[ v(\a^{jn}-1)=v(\a^{n}-1)+v(\F_{j-1}(\a^n))\ge v(\a^{n}-1) \] for any algebraic integer~$\a$ and any nonarchimedean absolute value~$v$.
nodes.statement_short: Factoring $X^{jn}-1=(X^n-1)\F_{j-1}(X^n)$ gives $v(\a^{jn}-1)\ge v(\a^n-1)$ at every nonarchimedean $v$.
nodes.section: 1 A Reformulation of Property

nodes.name: Summation and normalization
nodes.statement: Summing over $\a\in\Acal$ and $v\mid m$, and then dividing by~$n\log m$, gives the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Sum over $\a\in\Acal$ and $v\mid m$ and divide by $n\log m$.
nodes.section: 1 A Reformulation of Property

nodes.name: Setup: choose $\a_v$ inside the unit disk
nodes.statement: Let~$K$ be a number field such that $\Acal\subset K$. For~$\a\in\Acal$ and~$v\in M_K$, we let \[ \a_v = \begin{cases} \a&\text{if $\|\a\|_v\le1$,}\\ \a^{-1}&\text{if $\|\a\|_v>1$,}\\ \end{cases} \] so in particular $\|\a_v\|_v\le 1$.
nodes.statement_short: Replace $\a$ by $\a^{-1}$ where necessary so that $\|\a_v\|_v\le1$ at every place.
nodes.section: 2 A Height Bound for Polynomials Satisfying Congruence Conditions

nodes.name: Main chain of inequalities for $(n\log m)\D(\Acal,m,n)$
nodes.statement_short: Use integrality and the product rule to bound $(n\log m)\D$ by $n\sum h(\a)$ plus archimedean terms.
nodes.section: 2 A Height Bound for Polynomials Satisfying Congruence Conditions

nodes.name: Replace $\Acal$ by $\Acal^j$
nodes.statement: We now replace~$\Acal$ with~$\Acal^j$. Then using $h(\a^j)=jh(\a)$ and Proposition~\ref{prop:DAjmngeDAmn}, which says that $\D(\Acal,m,n)\le\D(\Acal^j,m,n)$, we find that \[ (n\log m)\D(\Acal,m,n) \le nj\sum_{\a\in\Acal}h(\a) + \sum_{\a\in\Acal}\sum_{v\in M_K^\infty} \log\|\a_v^{jn}-1\|_v . \]
nodes.statement_short: Apply the same computation to $\Acal^j$, using $h(\a^j)=jh(\a)$ and monotonicity of $\D$.
nodes.section: 2 A Height Bound for Polynomials Satisfying Congruence Conditions

nodes.name: Average against the Fej\'er multiplier
nodes.statement: We multiply by the Fej\'er multiplier $1-\frac{j}{J+1}$ and sum over $1\le j\le J$ to obtain \begin{multline*} \frac{Jn\log m}{2}\D(\Acal,m,n) \le \frac{(J^2+2J)n}{6}\sum_{\a\in\Acal}h(\a) \\* + \sum_{\a\in\Acal}\sum_{v\in M_K^\infty} \sum_{j=1}^J \left(1-\frac{j}{J+1}\right)\log\|\a_v^{jn}-1\|_v . \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Multiply by $1-\frac{j}{J+1}$ and sum over $1\le j\le J$.
nodes.section: 2 A Height Bound for Polynomials Satisfying Congruence Conditions

nodes.name: Bound the archimedean terms by a supremum over the unit disk
nodes.statement: Note that the sum over~$v$ is over archimedean absolute values, so if we assume that~$\a_v$ is chosen in the unit disk to maximize the innermost sum over~$j$, we get the estimate \begin{multline*} \frac{Jn\log m}{2}\D(\Acal,m,n) \\* \le \frac{(J^2+2J)n}{6}\sum_{\a\in\Acal}h(\a) + |\Acal| \sup_{\substack{z\in\CC\\|z|\le1\\}} \sum_{j=1}^J \left(1-\frac{j}{J+1}\right)\log|z^j-1|. \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Replace the innermost sum by its supremum over $|z|\le1$.
nodes.section: 2 A Height Bound for Polynomials Satisfying Congruence Conditions

nodes.name: Apply the Fejér kernel estimate and conclude
nodes.statement: We can now use Proposition~\ref{prop:fejarestimate} to conclude that \[ \frac{Jn\log m}{2}\D(\Acal,m,n) \le \frac{(J^2+2J)n}{6}\sum_{\a\in\Acal}h(\a) + \frac{|\Acal|}{2}\left(\log\left(\frac{J}{2}+1\right)+1\right). \] After a little bit of algebra, we obtain the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Insert the Fej\'er kernel bound and rearrange to get the stated inequality.
nodes.section: 2 A Height Bound for Polynomials Satisfying Congruence Conditions

nodes.name: Substitute $\D(\Acal_f,m,n)\ge(n-1)/n$ into the main theorem
nodes.statement: Let~$\Acal_f$ be the set of roots of~$f$. As noted in Remark~\ref{remark:DAfmD1geDD1}, the divisibility condition on~$f$ implies that $\D(\Acal_f,m,n)\ge (n-1)/n$. Substituting this into~\eqref{eqn:sumhageDAmnlogm} of Theorem~\ref{thm:hageCDAmnlogm} and using~$|\Acal_f|=D$, we find that for all integers $J\ge1$ we have \begin{align*} \sum_{f(\a)=0}h(\a) &\ge \frac{3}{J+2} \left(\frac{n-1}{n}\log m - \frac{D}{n}\frac{\log(J/2+1)+1}{J}\right). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Feed the divisibility bound of Remark~\ref{remark:DAfmD1geDD1} into the height inequality with $|\Acal_f|=D$.
nodes.section: 2 A Height Bound for Polynomials Satisfying Congruence Conditions

nodes.name: Weaken the constants for $n\ge2$ and $J\ge2$
nodes.statement: Since we are not concerned with optimizing our constants, we observe that for $n\ge2$ and $J\ge2$, this implies that \begin{equation} \sum_{f(\a)=0}h(\a) \ge \frac{1}{J} \left(\frac{1}{2}\log m - \frac{4D}{n}\frac{\log(J)}{J}\right). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Simplify to $\sum h(\a)\ge\frac1J(\frac12\log m-\frac{4D}{n}\frac{\log J}{J})$.
nodes.section: 2 A Height Bound for Polynomials Satisfying Congruence Conditions

nodes.name: Case $\log m\ge D/16n$
nodes.statement: We now consider two cases. First, if~$m$ is large, say \[ \log m \ge D/16n, \] then taking~$J=57$ gives \begin{equation} \sum_{f(\a)=0}h(\a) \ge \frac{1}{J}\left(\frac12-4\frac{\log(J)}{J}\right)\log m \ge \frac{\log m}{264}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Take $J=57$ to obtain $\sum h(\a)\ge(\log m)/264$.
nodes.section: 2 A Height Bound for Polynomials Satisfying Congruence Conditions

nodes.name: Case $\log m\le D/16n$
nodes.statement: Second, suppose that~$m$ is small, \[ \log m \le D/16n. \] Then we want to choose~$J$ to be an integer satisfying \begin{equation} \frac{J}{\log J} \ge \frac{16D}{n\log m}. \end{equation} In particular, since $16D/n\log m\ge256$, it suffices to take \[ J = \left\lfloor \frac{32D}{n\log m}\log\left(\frac{16D}{n\log m}\right) \right\rfloor - 1. \] Substituting~\eqref{eqn:JlogJge16dnlogm} into~\eqref{eqn:1J12m4DnlogJJ} and adjusting the constants yields \begin{equation} \sum_{f(\a)=0}h(\a) \ge \frac{\log m}{4J} \ge \frac{\log m}{(128D/n\log m)\log(16D/n\log m)}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Choose $J\approx\frac{32D}{n\log m}\log\frac{16D}{n\log m}$ to obtain the second bound.
nodes.section: 2 A Height Bound for Polynomials Satisfying Congruence Conditions

nodes.name: Combine the two cases
nodes.statement: Combining~\eqref{eqn:bd1} and~\eqref{eqn:bd2} completes the proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:htgeelogm}.
nodes.statement_short: Merge the two bounds into the stated case formula.
nodes.section: 2 A Height Bound for Polynomials Satisfying Congruence Conditions

nodes.name: Large-$m$ case handled by the lemma
nodes.statement: We are given that $n\ge\max\{\e D,2\}$. If $\log m\ge D/16n$, then Lemma~\ref{lemma:htgeelogm} says that \[ \sum_{f(\a)=0}h(\a) \ge \frac{\log m}{264}. \]
nodes.statement_short: If $\log m\ge D/16n$ the lemma already gives $(\log m)/264$.
nodes.section: 2 A Height Bound for Polynomials Satisfying Congruence Conditions

nodes.name: Reduce to the small-$m$ case and bound $D/n\log m$
nodes.statement: This is stronger than~\eqref{eqn:logm185e}, since we have assumed that $\e\le1$, so we are reduced to the case that~$\log m\le D/16n$. Since $n\ge\e D$, this implies that \[ \frac{D}{n\log m}\le\frac{D}{\e D\log m} \le \frac{1}{\e\log m}, \] where the upper bound is at least~$16$.
nodes.statement_short: Use $\e\le1$ and $n\ge\e D$ to get $D/(n\log m)\le1/(\e\log m)$.
nodes.section: 2 A Height Bound for Polynomials Satisfying Congruence Conditions

nodes.name: Conclude the explicit bound
nodes.statement: Substituting this into Lemma~\ref{lemma:htgeelogm}, we find that \[ \sum_{f(\a)=0}h(\a) \ge \frac{\log m}{(128/\e\log m)\log(16/\e\log m)}. \] Since~$m\ge2$, this gives something slightly stronger than the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Substitute back to obtain something slightly stronger than the stated bound.
nodes.section: 2 A Height Bound for Polynomials Satisfying Congruence Conditions

nodes.name: Lower bound for the local height (first part of (a))
nodes.statement: The first part of~(a) follows from~\cite[Theorem~VI.1.1(a)]{ATAEC}, which says in particular that~$\lhat_v$ has a logarithmic pole as $P\to O$ in the $v$-adic topology and that~$\l_v$ is bounded on the complement of any $v$-adic neighborhood of~$O$.
nodes.statement_short: Cite the logarithmic pole of $\lhat_v$ at $O$ and its boundedness elsewhere.
nodes.section: 3 An Elliptic Analogue of $\D(\Acal,m,n)$
nodes.origin_citation: Silverman, ATAEC, Theorems VI.1.1, VI.4.1, VI.2.1

nodes.name: Non-negativity at good reduction (second part of (a))
nodes.statement: The second part of~(a) follow from~\cite[Theorem~VI.4.1]{ATAEC}, which says that if~$P$ reduces to a non-singular point modulo~$v$, then \[ \lhat_v(P) = \frac12\max\bigl\{-v\bigl(x(P)\bigr),0\bigr\} +\frac1{12}v(\gD_{E/K}). \] This quantity is clearly non-negative.
nodes.statement_short: The explicit good-reduction formula for $\lhat_v$ is visibly non-negative.
nodes.section: 3 An Elliptic Analogue of $\D(\Acal,m,n)$
nodes.origin_citation: Silverman, ATAEC, Theorems VI.1.1, VI.4.1, VI.2.1

nodes.name: Decomposition of the global height (part (b))
nodes.statement: Finally, \cite[Theorem~VI.2.1]{ATAEC} gives a proof of~(b).
nodes.statement_short: Quote the sum-of-local-heights theorem.
nodes.section: 3 An Elliptic Analogue of $\D(\Acal,m,n)$
nodes.origin_citation: Silverman, ATAEC, Theorems VI.1.1, VI.4.1, VI.2.1

nodes.name: Reduce to good reduction and set up the formal group filtration
nodes.statement: Replacing~$K$ by a finite extension, we may assume that~$E$ has good reduction at all primes dividing~$\gm$. Let~$v\in M_K^0$ be any place at which~$E$ has good reduction, and let~$\pi_v\in K$ be a uniformizer at~$v$. Further, let \[ E_0(\Kbar_v) \subset E_1(\Kbar_v) \subset E_2(\Kbar_v) \subset \cdots \] be the formal group filtration of~$E(\Kbar_v)$; see~\cite[Chapters~IV,~VII]{MR2514094}. Here $E_0=E$, since we have assumed good reduction, and~$E_1$ is the formal group.
nodes.statement_short: Enlarge $K$ so that $E$ has good reduction at all $v\mid\gm$ and introduce $E_0\subset E_1\subset\cdots$.
nodes.section: 3 An Elliptic Analogue of $\D(\Acal,m,n)$

nodes.name: Monotonicity $\lhat_v(jP)\ge\lhat_v(P)$
nodes.statement: The explicit formula for~$\lhat_v$~\cite[Theorem~VI.4.1]{ATAEC} then has the form \[ \lhat_v(P) = \max\bigl\{r\ge0 : P \in E_r(\Kbar_v)\bigr\}v(\pi_v). \] Since the filtration consists of subgroups, it is immediate that \[ \lhat_v(jP) \ge \lhat_v(P) \qquad\text{for all $j\ge1$.} \]
nodes.statement_short: The filtration formula for $\lhat_v$ plus the subgroup property gives monotonicity under multiplication by $j$.
nodes.section: 3 An Elliptic Analogue of $\D(\Acal,m,n)$

nodes.name: Sum and normalize
nodes.statement: Summing over $P\in\Pcal$ and $v\mid\gm$, and dividing by $n^2\log m$, the desired result is immediate from the definition of~$\D$.
nodes.statement_short: Sum over $P\in\Pcal$ and $v\mid\gm$ and divide by $n^2\log m$.
nodes.section: 3 An Elliptic Analogue of $\D(\Acal,m,n)$

nodes.name: Nonarchimedean places of good reduction
nodes.statement: If~$v$ is nonarchimedean and~$E$ has good reduction at~$v$, then the local height~$\lhat_v$ is non-negative, so we can take $c_1(v)=c_2(v)=0$.
nodes.statement_short: $\lhat_v\ge0$ there, so both constants may be taken to be $0$.
nodes.section: 4 A Height Lower Bound for Points on Elliptic Curves

nodes.name: Nonarchimedean places of bad reduction
nodes.statement: For nonarchimedean~$v$ of bad reduction, the inequality~\eqref{eqn:fejarjPgec1v} with $c_1(v)=0$ is proven in~\cite{HiSi2}.
nodes.statement_short: Quote the corresponding inequality with $c_1(v)=0$ from Hindry-Silverman.
nodes.section: 4 A Height Lower Bound for Points on Elliptic Curves

nodes.name: Archimedean places via Elkies' theorem
nodes.statement: Finally, for archimedean~$v$, the local height functions are Green's functions and the desired result follows from a general theorem of Elkies~\cite[Theorem~5.1]{LangAT} that is valid on curves of positive genus. More precisely, Elkies' theorem says that there is a constant $c=c(E,v)$ such that for any distinct points~$P_0,\ldots,P_J\in E(K_v)$ we have \begin{equation} \sum_{0\le i<j\le J} \lhat_v(P_j-P_i) \ge -\frac{1}{2\pi}(J+1)\log J - cJ. \end{equation} (We are using the fact that~$\lhat_v$ is an even function.)
nodes.statement_short: Green's-function lower bound for distinct points on a curve of positive genus.
nodes.section: 4 A Height Lower Bound for Points on Elliptic Curves

nodes.name: Specialize to $P_j=jP$ and combine
nodes.statement: Taking $P_j=jP$ for $0\le j\le J$, we find that \begin{equation} \sum_{0\le i<j\le J} \lhat_v(P_j-P_i) = \sum_{0\le i<j\le J} \lhat_v\bigl((j-i)P\bigr) = \sum_{j=1}^J (J+1-j)\lhat_v(jP). \end{equation} Combining~\eqref{eqn1} and~\eqref{eqn2} and dividing by~$J+1$ gives~\eqref{eqn:fejarjPgec1v}.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the double sum as $\sum_j(J+1-j)\lhat_v(jP)$ and divide by $J+1$.
nodes.section: 4 A Height Lower Bound for Points on Elliptic Curves

nodes.name: Fej\'er weights $f_j$ and their moments $F_0,F_2$
nodes.statement: To ease notation, we let \[ f_j = 1-\frac{j}{J+1} \qquad\text{and}\qquad F_k = \sum_{j=1}^J j^kf_j. \] Earlier we used the values of~$F_0$ and~$F_1$. In this section we will use the values \begin{equation} F_0 = \frac{J}{2} \qquad\text{and}\qquad F_2 = \frac{J(J+1)(J+2)}{12}. \end{equation} \par
nodes.statement_short: Set $f_j=1-\frac{j}{J+1}$ and record $F_0=J/2$, $F_2=J(J+1)(J+2)/12$.
nodes.section: 4 A Height Lower Bound for Points on Elliptic Curves

nodes.name: Reduce to $\Pcal\subset E(K)$ and isolate the bad places
nodes.statement: Replacing~$K$ by a finite extension, we may assume that~$\Pcal\subset E(K)$. We let \[ M_K^\bad = M_K^\infty \cup \{v\in M_K^0 : \text{$E$ has bad reduction at $v$}\} . \] Then \[ v\in M_K\setminus M_K^\bad \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \l_v(Q)\ge0\quad\text{for all $Q\in E(\Kbar_v)$.} \] \par
nodes.statement_short: Enlarge $K$ and define $M_K^\bad$, off which all local heights are non-negative.
nodes.section: 4 A Height Lower Bound for Points on Elliptic Curves

nodes.name: Decompose $n^2\sum\hhat(P)$ into local heights
nodes.statement: We compute \begin{align*} n^2\sum_{P\in\Pcal} \hhat(P) & = \sum_{P\in\Pcal} \hhat(nP) \\ & = \sum_{P\in\Pcal} \sum_{v\in M_K} \lhat_v(nP) \\ &\ge \sum_{P\in\Pcal} \sum_{v\mid\gm} \lhat_v(nP) + \sum_{P\in\Pcal} \sum_{v\in M_K^\bad} \lhat_v(nP) \\ &= (n^2\log m)\D(\Pcal,\gm,n) + \sum_{P\in\Pcal} \sum_{v\in M_K^\bad} \lhat_v(nP). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Split the sum of local heights into the places above $\gm$ and the bad places.
nodes.section: 4 A Height Lower Bound for Points on Elliptic Curves

nodes.name: Replace $\Pcal$ by $j\Pcal$
nodes.statement: Replacing~$\Pcal$ with $j\Pcal=\{jP:P\in\Pcal\}$ and using Lemma~\ref{lemma:DjPgeDP}, which says that $\D(j\Pcal,\gm,n)\ge\D(\Pcal,\gm,n)$ (this is where we use the assumption that~$E$ has potential good reduction at the primes dividing~$\gm$), we find that \[ n^2j^2\sum_{P\in\Pcal} \hhat(P) \ge (n^2\log m)\D(\Pcal,\gm,n) + \sum_{P\in\Pcal} \sum_{v\in M_K^\bad} \lhat_v(njP). \]
nodes.statement_short: Potential good reduction gives $\D(j\Pcal,\gm,n)\ge\D(\Pcal,\gm,n)$.
nodes.section: 4 A Height Lower Bound for Points on Elliptic Curves

nodes.name: Average against $f_j$
nodes.statement: Multiplying both sides by~$f_j$ and summing $j=1$ to~$J$ gives \begin{align*} F_2n^2\sum_{P\in\Pcal}& \hhat(P)\\ &\ge F_0(n^2\log m)\D(\Pcal,\gm,n) + \sum_{j=1}^J \sum_{P\in\Pcal} \sum_{v\in M_K^\bad} f_j\lhat_v(njP) \\ &\ge F_0(n^2\log m)\D(\Pcal,\gm,n) + |\Pcal|\sum_{v\in M_K^\bad} \inf_{Q\in E(K)} \sum_{j=1}^J f_j\lhat_v(jQ). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Multiply by $f_j$, sum over $j$, and bound the bad-place terms by an infimum over $Q$.
nodes.section: 4 A Height Lower Bound for Points on Elliptic Curves

nodes.name: Bound the bad-place terms by the Fourier averaging estimate
nodes.statement: Proposition~\ref{prop:fourieravg} says that there are~$M_K$-constants~$c_1$ and~$c_2$, depending only on~$E$, such that \[ \inf_{Q\in E(K)} \sum_{j=1}^J f_j\lhat_v(jQ) \ge -c_1(v)\log(J)-c_2(v). \] Summing over $v\in M_K^\bad$ gives constants that depend only on~$E$, so adjusting the constants and using the assumption that $J\ge1$, we find that there is a constant~$C_E$, depending only on~$E$, such that \[ F_2n^2\sum_{P\in\Pcal} \hhat(P) \ge F_0(n^2\log m)\D(\Pcal,\gm,n) -C_E |\Pcal|\log(J+1). \]
nodes.statement_short: Absorb the $M_K$-constants $c_1,c_2$ into a single constant $C_E$.
nodes.section: 4 A Height Lower Bound for Points on Elliptic Curves

nodes.name: Divide by $F_2n^2$ and conclude
nodes.statement: Using the formulas~\eqref{eqn:F0F1F2} for~$F_0$ and~$F_2$, dividing by~$F_2n^2$, and adjusting the constant gives the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: Insert the values of $F_0$ and $F_2$ to obtain the stated inequality.
nodes.section: 4 A Height Lower Bound for Points on Elliptic Curves

nodes.name: Insert the hypotheses into the elliptic height bound
nodes.statement: We are given that $n\ge\sqrt{\e D_Q}$ and $\D(\Pcal_Q,\gm,n)\ge\d$. Using these values in Theorem~\ref{thm:sumhhatPgeD} together with some trivial estimates yields \[ \sum_{P\in\Pcal_Q}\hhat(P) \ge \frac{1}{J^2}\left(\d\log m -\frac{C_E}{\e}\cdot\frac{\log(J+1)}{J}\right). \]
nodes.statement_short: Use $n\ge\sqrt{\e D_Q}$ and $\D(\Pcal_Q,\gm,n)\ge\d$ plus trivial estimates.
nodes.section: 4 A Height Lower Bound for Points on Elliptic Curves

nodes.name: Choose $J$
nodes.statement: We now choose~$J$ to be the smallest integer satisfying \[ \frac{\log(J+1)}{J} \le \min\left\{ \frac{\e\d}{2C_E}\log m, \frac12\right\}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Take the least $J$ with $\log(J+1)/J\le\min\{\e\d\log m/2C_E,\tfrac12\}$.
nodes.section: 4 A Height Lower Bound for Points on Elliptic Curves

nodes.name: Conclude the elliptic Lehmer bound
nodes.statement: This yields an estimate of the desired form \[ D_Q\hhat(Q) \ge C_{E/K,\d,\e}\log m, \] where we are using the fact, noted earlier, that every point in~$\Pcal_Q$ has canonical height equal to~$\hhat(Q)$.
nodes.statement_short: All conjugates of $Q$ share the same canonical height, giving $D_Q\hhat(Q)\ge C_{E/K,\d,\e}\log m$.
nodes.section: 4 A Height Lower Bound for Points on Elliptic Curves

nodes.name: Factor the resultant of $f$ with $X^{D+1}-1+(X-1)u(X)$
nodes.statement: We are given that \[ f(X) = \F_D(X) + u(X) + mr(X) \qquad\text{for some $r(X)\in\ZZ[X]$.} \] Then \begin{align*} \Resultant\bigl(f(X)&,X^{D+1}-1+(X-1)u(X)\bigr)\\* &= \Resultant\bigl(f(X),\F_D(X)+u(X)\bigr) \cdot\Resultant\bigl(f(X),X-1\bigr) \\ &= \Resultant\bigl(mr(X),\F_D(X)+u(X)\bigr)f(1) \\ &= m^D\Resultant\bigl(r(X),\F_D(X)+u(X)\bigr)f(1). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Write $f=\F_D+u+mr$ and pull the factor $m^D$ out of the resultant.
nodes.section: 5 Other Congruence Conditions on the Coefficients

nodes.name: Bound $D\log m$ by archimedean contributions
nodes.statement:
By assumption, the resultants are nonzero integers, so we find that  egin{align} D\log m &\le \log\left|\Resultant igl(f(X),X^{D+1}-1+(X-1)u(X) igr)ight| 
otag\ &= \sum_{f(\a)=0} \sum_{v\in M_K^\infty} \log\|\a^{D+1}-1+(\a-1)u(\a)\|_v 
otag\ &= \sum_{v\in M_K^\infty}\sum_{\substack{f(\a)=0\\|\a\|_v>1\}} \log\|\a^{D+1}\|_v 
otag\ &\qquad{} + \sum_{v\in M_K^\infty}\sum_{\substack{f(\a)=0\\|\a\|_v>1\}} \log\left\| rac{\a^{D+1}-1+(\a-1)u(\a)}{\a^{D+1}}ight\|_v 
otag\ &\qquad{} + \sum_{v\in M_K^\infty}\sum_{\substack{f(\a)=0\\|\a\|_v\le1\}} \log\|\a^{D+1}-1+(\a-1)u(\a)\|_v 
otag\ &\le h(\a^{D+1}) + D\sup_{|z|=1}\log igl|z^{D+1}-1+(z-1)u(z) igr| \ &\le (D+1)h(\a) + D\log L igl(X^{D+1}-1+(X-1)u(X) igr). 
otag \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Expand $\log|\Resultant|$ over archimedean places, splitting by $\|\a\|_v>1$ or $\le1$.
nodes.section: 5 Other Congruence Conditions on the Coefficients

nodes.name: Reduce the supremum to the unit circle
nodes.statement: (We note that in \eqref{eqn:DlogmaD1DLX}, it suffices to take the supremum over~$|z|=1$, since $\log|w|$ is harmonic inside the unit disk.)
nodes.statement_short: Harmonicity of $\log|w|$ lets the supremum be taken over $|z|=1$.
nodes.section: 5 Other Congruence Conditions on the Coefficients

nodes.name: Introduce the difference function $F_t(\theta)$
nodes.statement: For notational convenience we let \[ F_t(\theta) = \log|1-e^{-t}e^{i\theta}| + \frac12t - \log|1-e^{i\theta}|, \] so we need to prove that $F_t(\theta)\ge0$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce the claim to showing $F_t(\theta)\ge0$.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Proposition

nodes.name: Base value $F_0(\theta)=0$
nodes.statement: We have \[ F_0(\theta)=0 \qquad\text{for all $\theta\in\RR\setminus2\pi i\ZZ$.} \]
nodes.statement_short: The inequality is an equality at $t=0$.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Proposition

nodes.name: Positivity of $\partial F_t/\partial t$
nodes.statement: For $t>0$ we observe that \[ \log|1-e^{-t}e^{i\theta}| = \Re\biggl(\sum_{n=1}^\infty -\frac{e^{-nt}e^{in\theta}}{n}\biggr) \] is given by an absolutely convergent series, so we may differentiate it term-by-term. Hence \begin{align*} \frac{\partial F_t}{\partial t}(\theta) &= \Re\biggl(\sum_{n=1}^\infty (e^{-t+i\theta})^n\biggr) + \frac12 = \Re\left( \frac{e^{-t+i\theta}}{1-e^{-t+i\theta}}\right) + \frac12 \\ &= \frac{e^{2t}-1}{(e^t-\cos\theta)^2+\sin^2\theta} > 0 \qquad\text{for all $t>0$.} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate the absolutely convergent log-series term-by-term.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Proposition

nodes.name: Conclude by monotonicity in $t$
nodes.statement: Thus for any fixed $\theta\in\RR\setminus2\pi i\ZZ$, the function~$F_t(\theta)$ as a function of~$t\ge0$ satisfies~$F_0(\theta)=0$ and~$(\partial F_t/\partial t)(\theta)\ge 0$. Hence~$F_t(\theta)\ge0$ for all $t\ge0$.
nodes.statement_short: $F_0=0$ together with a non-negative $t$-derivative forces $F_t(\theta)\ge0$.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Proposition

nodes.name: Reduce to the unit circle by harmonicity
nodes.statement: The functions $\log|1-z^j|$ are harmonic on the open unit disk $|z|<1$, so the maximum occurs on the boundary.
nodes.statement_short: The functions $\log|1-z^j|$ are harmonic on $|z|<1$, so the maximum is on the boundary.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Proposition

nodes.name: Fourier expansion into a Fejér kernel
nodes.statement: For $z=e^{i\theta}$ on the unit circle we estimate \begin{align*} \sum_{j=1}^J&\left(1-\frac{j}{J+1}\right)\log|1-z^j|\\ &\le \sum_{j=1}^J \left(1-\frac{j}{J+1}\right) \left(\log|1-e^{-t}e^{ij\theta}| + \frac12t\right) &&\text{from Lemma \ref{lemma:Gttheta},} \\ &= \Re\biggl( \sum_{j=1}^J \left(1-\frac{j}{J+1}\right) \sum_{k=1}^\infty -\frac{e^{-kt}e^{ijk\theta}}{k} \biggr) + \frac{Jt}{4} \\ &= \Re\biggl( \sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac{e^{-kt}}{k}\sum_{j=1}^J -\left(1-\frac{j}{J+1}\right)e^{ijk\theta} \biggr)+ \frac{Jt}{4} \\ &= \sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac{e^{-kt}}{k} \biggl(\frac12 -\frac{1}{2J+2}\biggl|\sum_{j=0}^Je^{ijk\theta}\biggr|^2\biggr) + \frac{Jt}{4} \hidewidth\\ &\ge \sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac{e^{-kt}}{2k} + \frac{Jt}{4} \\ &= -\frac12\log(1-e^{-t}) + \frac{Jt}{4}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the damping lemma, expand the logarithm, and recognize $|\sum_{j=0}^Je^{ijk\theta}|^2$.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Proposition

nodes.name: Optimize $t=\log(1+2J^{-1})$
nodes.statement: This estimate holds for all $t>0$, so in particular we can set $t=\log(1+2J^{-1})$, which (after some algebra) gives the estimate \[ \sum_{j=1}^J f_j\log|1-z^j| \le \frac12\log\left(\frac{J}{2}+1\right) +\frac{J}{4}\log\left(1+\frac{2}{J}\right). \]
nodes.statement_short: Choose $t$ to balance the two terms in the bound.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Proposition

nodes.name: Conclude via $x\log(1+x^{-1})\le1$
nodes.statement: Finally we observe that $x\log(1+x^{-1})\le 1$ for all $x\ge0$, which gives the desired result.
nodes.statement_short: A final elementary inequality yields the stated estimate.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Proposition
